abstract: A recurring objection to emergent approaches is that if the underlying theory is deterministic, then the emergent effective theory must also be deterministic; conversely, if the effective theory is stochastic, it must be merely random. We show that both inferences fail in Modal Triplet Theory (MTT). In MTT, the coherent projector is non-invertible and stabilization is contractive on admissible domains. We prove: (i) determinism does not descend to the 4D coherent effective theory unless a stringent fiber-invariance condition holds; (ii) the induced 4D stochastic evolution is not random but is geometrically biased and bounded by admissibility through a selection potential \Xi and an OU-type damping–disturbance balance; and (iii) once an outcome/commitment is selected, coupled coherent subsystems undergo cascading basin reconfiguration that quenches downstream variability. This yields a third category of dynamics: lawful stochasticity generated by deterministic micro-evolution plus information-erasing stabilization. We clarify why this differs from superdeterminism and why many other theories do not naturally realize the same trichotomy.
